title: A Thorn for the Garden Again
premise: Vesper Blackwood, a mercenary bound by oath to a god who has gone silent, keeps the ledgers of the Gilded Thorn, a guild that trades in impossible things — bottled memories, borrowed luck, second chances. When the border wards collapse on the same night every star goes out, Vesper discovers her guildmaster sold his own soul to the Undercourt beneath the mountain to buy the guild's survival, and the long winter now falling is the price coming due. To save him, she must steal that soul back from a court of exiled gods, aided by a disgraced ward-smith, a debt-collector ghost, and a found family she never meant to love. In the end Vesper learns her silent god never abandoned her — it became the wards themselves — and she must choose between restoring the stars or keeping her guildmaster alive; she finds a third path, paying the debt with her own name, becoming both ledger and keeper as winter breaks.
about_author: Theo Eriksen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval trade ledgers before turning to fantasy. They write stories about people who keep accounts — of money, of oaths, of the heart.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A quiet night at the Gilded Thorn: she audits entries for a bottled memory and a stolen shadow, trading barbs with guildmaster Corvane Ash. Establishes her dry competence and her nightly ritual of praying to her silent god. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as routine.

chapters.title: A God Who Stopped Answering
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Flashback woven through present: how she swore herself to Vael, god of thresholds, at fifteen after he saved her from slavers — and how ten years of silence have hollowed the oath. Corvane notices her doubt. Emotional beat: grief for a faith that may have been one-sided all along.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The stars vanish mid-sentence; the border wards shatter like glass; something vast moves beneath the mountain. The guild's impossible inventory begins leaking its power. Corvane goes pale and gives an order he's never given: seal the vaults. Emotional beat: dread arriving like weather.

chapters.title: What Corvane Buried in the Books
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Auditing the panic, Vesper finds a ledger page written in her own hand that she never wrote — dated three years hence. It names the Undercourt and a soul sold. She confronts Corvane; he refuses to explain. Emotional beat: betrayal cracking the found family's foundation.

chapters.title: The Ward-Smith Who Fell
chapters.summary: Ilsa Rennick's POV. Introduce Ilsa, a disgraced ward-smith drinking away her shame in a border town when the wards she once maintained fail. Vesper arrives to hire the only person who understands what broke. Their first meeting is a knife-fight that becomes a negotiation. Emotional beat: two proud women recognizing each other's damage.

chapters.title: Terms of Debt
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The deal is struck: Ilsa will rebuild a road into the mountain if Vesper clears her name with the Wardens' Guild. Corvane finally confesses partially — he owes the Undercourt, but not what or why. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance built on mutual leverage.

chapters.title: The Ghost Who Collects
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. Bramble, a debt-collector ghost bound to the Thorn's oldest contract, attaches himself to Vesper's expedition because her quest voids his binding. Comic, melancholy voice; he knows the Undercourt from the inside. Emotional beat: humor as armor over centuries of servitude.

chapters.title: Road Through the Long Winter
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The party travels through a land where winter falls upward and snow remembers the shapes of the dead. First Undercourt scouts attack — courtiers made of frost and courtesy. Ilsa saves Vesper's life; trust begins. Emotional beat: found family forming under pressure.

chapters.title: The Inn at the Edge of the Map
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Shelter in an inn that exists only while someone tells a true story inside it. Around the fire, each character shares a truth; Bramble reveals the Undercourt trades in souls the way the Thorn trades in everything else — and that Corvane's soul was collateral, not payment. Emotional beat: intimacy earned through honesty.

chapters.title: Threshold
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. At the mountain gate, Vesper prays to Vael out of habit — and for the first time in ten years, feels something answer: a single word, 'descend.' Hope and terror in equal measure. They enter the Undercourt. Emotional beat: faith rekindling at the worst possible moment.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. A tour of the Undercourt: exiled gods playing politics with mortal souls as currency, ballrooms carved from geodes, etiquette enforced by entropy. Vesper poses as a broker from the Gilded Thorn. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into horror at what immortality does to the powerful.

chapters.title: An Audience with the Pale Regent
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The Pale Regent, an exiled goddess of endings, receives them. She reveals the truth: Corvane sold his soul to buy the guild a century ago, but the debt has compounded — and the falling winter is the collection notice. She offers Vesper a bargain. Emotional beat: the enemy is reasonable, which is worse.

chapters.title: The Price of a Century
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV (interlude). Backstory chapter: young Corvane founding the Thorn, desperate, making the deal, and spending a hundred years pretending the silence in his chest wasn't guilt. Ends with him sealing the guild vaults and walking toward the mountain alone. Emotional beat: sympathy for a man who thought he was protecting everyone.

chapters.title: Ledger Entries, Forged and True
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper discovers the future-dated page in her own hand was written by the Regent — a trap to lure her, because a soul sworn to a god can be used to unmake the wards permanently. Her identity as Vael's sworn blade makes her the key. Emotional beat: realizing she isn't the rescuer; she's the prize.

chapters.title: The Vault of Names
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Heist preparation: the soul-vault where the Undercourt stores its holdings, warded by Ilsa's own estranged mentor. Ilsa must face the woman who cast her out. Old wounds reopened; new plan forged. Emotional beat: reconciliation as strategy and as grace.

chapters.title: Stealing Back a Soul
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The heist itself — misdirection, forged contracts, Bramble haunting the ledgers literally. They find Corvane's soul: a small, dim flame that recognizes Vesper and flinches. Extraction succeeds until the alarms of the court wake. Emotional beat: tenderness toward something fragile and guilty.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Geode Halls
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. The Regent springs her trap: she never needed Vesper caught — she needed Vesper's god to answer, and it did. Vael's presence in Vesper becomes a beacon that will crack the last wards. One ally turns coat to save their own binding. Escape through collapsing halls. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against self-preservation.

chapters.title: What the Silence Was
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Cornered, Vesper finally hears Vael fully: her god didn't go silent — it poured itself into the border wards generations ago, and every sworn mercenary since has been unknowingly holding the world together. The stars went out because Vael is nearly spent. Emotional beat: devastating reframing of abandonment as sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Bargain at the End of Winter
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Climax. Confrontation with the Pale Regent as the long winter reaches the mountain's heart. Vesper offers the third path: her name struck from every ledger, god-ledger included — she becomes the new threshold, the living ward, if the Regent cancels the debt and releases the hoarded souls. The Regent, tired of exile, accepts. Emotional beat: self-sacrifice chosen freely, not demanded.

chapters.title: Stars, Returning
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. The exchange: Vesper steps into the ward-lattice; the stars reignite one by one; winter halts mid-fall. Corvane, restored but diminished, carries her body home. Bramble's binding dissolves and he chooses, astonishingly, to stay anyway. Emotional beat: grief and awe entwined.

chapters.title: The Keeper of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Months later: the Thorn rebuilt, Ilsa reinstated, Corvane retired to teach. But Vesper persists within the wards — able to speak through thresholds, doorways, and open books. Not dead; changed. The family adapts around her new shape. Emotional beat: found family redefining itself rather than mourning.

chapters.title: A Thorn for the Garden Again
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, liminal. Final chapter in her half-divine voice: she tends the borders, whispers warnings through keyholes, and writes — in a hand only Ilsa can see — the first entry of a new ledger. The last line mirrors the book's first. Emotional beat: peace earned, identity transformed but intact.
